_about: Metric playground (Demos, brief 09). Text and presets for assets/js/playground.js. Wording from 6-evaluation.tex §6.1/§6.3 and A-appendix.tex sec:appendix-metrics. {cor_rnk_only} and {cor} are filled from data/papers.json sankey.headline at render time; {pos} {neg} {item} {items} {Pos} {Items} from the selected binary target.
title: Metric playground
lede: Ranking, calibration, scoring and decision metrics measure different aspects of the same uncertainty score. Faithfulness metrics need no ground truth: they measure the agreement between two uncertainty signals of the same model.
survey_line: In the survey, {cor_rnk_only} of {cor} correctness papers report ranking metrics only.
keys: Keyboard: left and right arrows move a point or τ by 0.01, with Shift by 0.1; in the faithfulness plot up and down move signal 2. N and P go to the next and previous point. L flips a point's label; Delete removes it.

COR.name: Correctness
COR.pdef: its confidence 1 − U is read as the predicted probability that the answer is correct

GRD.name: Grounding
GRD.pdef: 1 − U is read as the predicted probability that the answer is grounded

UNS.name: Underspecification
UNS.pdef: 1 − U is read as the predicted probability that the input is well specified

cor.sub: Each mark is one {item}: U runs from 0 (certain) to 1 (uncertain), {p} is the predicted probability that it is {pos}, and τ gives the decision d(x) = 1[U(x) < τ].
cor.moral: Ranking depends only on the order of the scores, whereas calibration depends on their values. Scoring rules reflect calibration and how concentrated the scores are, and a decision metric is a single operating point on a ranking curve. A score can do well in one family and badly in another.
cor.edited: Your own scores. Pick a preset to start again.

metrics.name: AUROC
metrics.gloss: P(a random {pos} {item} is less uncertain than a random {neg} one).

metrics.name: AURC
metrics.gloss: Mean share of {neg} {items} among the k least uncertain, k = 1 … n.

metrics.name: AUARC
metrics.gloss: Mean share of {pos} {items} among those retained; equals 1 − AURC.

metrics.name: AUPRC
metrics.gloss: Average precision, with {pos} {items} as the positive class.

metrics.name: PRR
metrics.gloss: Where AURC sits between random (0) and the oracle (1).

metrics.name: ECE
metrics.gloss: Gap between {p} and the share of {pos} {items}, in 10 bins.

metrics.name: MCE
metrics.gloss: The largest such gap over the 10 bins.

metrics.name: ACE
metrics.gloss: ECE with 10 bins of equal size instead of equal width.

metrics.name: Brier
metrics.gloss: Mean squared error between 1 − U and the label c.

metrics.name: Accuracy @ τ
metrics.gloss: Share of {items} where d = 1[U < τ] matches the label.

metrics.name: F1 @ τ
metrics.gloss: Harmonic mean of precision and recall of d at τ.

rel.title: Reliability diagram
rel.note: Bars: share of {pos} {items} per bin; the number above is the bin size. Diagonal: perfect calibration. Hatched: the gap between the mean of {p} (black tick) and that share.
rel.note_mce: Outlined: the worst bin, whose gap is the MCE.

ace.title: Reliability, equal-mass bins
ace.note: Dots: mean {p} and share of {pos} {items} in each equal-mass bin. Lines to the diagonal: the gaps that ACE averages.

roc.title: ROC curve
roc.note: Positive = {pos}; the threshold sweeps U from low to high. Shaded: AUROC. Dashed diagonal: random.

rc.title: Risk–coverage curve
rc.note: Shaded: AURC. Dashed: random order. Dotted: oracle (every {neg} {item} rejected first).

arc.title: Accuracy–rejection curve
arc.note: Shaded: AUARC = 1 − AURC. Dashed: random order. Dotted: oracle.

pr.title: Precision–recall curve
pr.note: Positive = {pos}. Shaded: average precision (AUPRC). Dashed: share of {pos} {items}, the random baseline.

presets.label: Good ranking, bad calibration
presets.caption: Every {pos} {item} is less uncertain than every {neg} one, so sorting by U puts all {pos} {items} first. But all scores sit below U = 0.1, so each says its {item} is at least 90% likely to be {pos}. Prediction and observed share disagree.

presets.label: Good calibration, bad ranking
presets.caption: Every {item} has U = 0.5, so 1 − U equals the observed share of {pos} {items} (10 of 20) and the prediction is right on average. But a constant score cannot tell {pos} from {neg}: sorting by U leaves them in any order, so the risk–coverage curve is the random line.

presets.label: Good uncertainty score
presets.caption: {Pos} {items} mostly sit at low U and {neg} ones at high U, so sorting by U puts most {pos} {items} first. Within each bin, the share of {pos} {items} is close to the predicted probability 1 − U, so the scores can be read as probabilities.

presets.label: Random uncertainty score
presets.caption: The scores are drawn independently of the label, so their order carries no information about which {items} are {pos}: {pos} and {neg} marks are spread evenly along the strip. The score is miscalibrated too.

real_data.label: Real data (TriviaQA)
real_data.caption: {n} TriviaQA questions answered by {model_full} ({model}), a stratified sample of the test split that keeps its error rate: {npos} answers are correct and {nneg} wrong. Each mark is one real answer.

msp.label: U = 1 − MSP
msp.note: MSP is the maximum softmax probability of the last token.

se.label: U = SE / ln 21
se.note: Semantic entropy over the greedy answer and 20 samples, divided by its largest value, ln 21. Calibration metrics (ECE, MCE, ACE, Brier) are not meaningful for a rescaled SE; ranking metrics are.

fth.sub: No ground truth: each dot is one answer, placed by two uncertainty signals of the same model (e.g., sampling consistency and verbalized confidence).

metrics.name: Rank correlation
metrics.gloss: Spearman correlation between the two signals.

metrics.name: cMFG
metrics.gloss: Mean of 1 − |signal 2 − signal 1| per bin of signal 1, then over bins.

fth.caption: Rank correlation depends only on the order of the two signals; cMFG depends on the gap between their values. Neither needs a correctness label.
fth.edited: Your own points. Pick a preset to start again.

presets.label: Faithful
presets.caption: The two signals agree: every dot sits on or next to the diagonal, so both signals give each answer the same order and nearly the same level. The thin vertical lines, the gaps between the two signals, are all short.

presets.label: Unfaithful
presets.caption: Signal 2 has nothing to do with signal 1: the dots are scattered over the plot. The order is lost, and the gaps between the two signals, the vertical lines to the diagonal, are large for most answers.

presets.label: Faithful in order only
presets.caption: Signal 2 rises with signal 1 but is squeezed into 0.57–0.94, so the dots form a flatter line above the diagonal. The order is identical, but the levels differ, most where signal 1 is low.

presets.label: Faithful in level only
presets.caption: Signal 2 stays within 0.12 of signal 1, so every dot is close to the diagonal and the gaps are short. But all answers sit at similar levels between 0.4 and 0.6, and within that band their order is scrambled.

linkout: Where these metrics sit in the protocol: target → criterion → metric, and which families the surveyed papers report.
